prompt: What did Bacchelli and Bird find about code review at Microsoft?

choices.text: Developers did not value review at all
choices.why: They valued it, for a reason other than the one it served.

choices.text: Knowledge transfer was a main outcome, though people expected bugs
choices.why: Right: developers said defects; the comments said readability, alternatives and understanding.

choices.text: Reviews caught most defects before release, as developers expected
choices.why: Defects were a minority of comments.

choices.text: Reviews were mostly about formatting
choices.why: Not their finding.

prompt: Of checkout's 140 review comments in June, how many caught something that would have been a bug?
Why does Diego's plan have him reviewing other people's pull requests?

choices.text: To reduce the load on Bruna, who reviews most of the team's code
choices.why: A side effect at most.

choices.text: So he can be measured on review count
choices.why: Nobody counts reviews in the plan; it records what he learns.

choices.text: Because juniors find more defects than seniors
choices.why: Not a claim the lesson makes.

choices.text: To learn the parts of the system he does not work on
choices.why: Right: reading code he did not write and asking about decisions.

prompt: Which does the lesson say review is not for? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Formatting a machine can check
choices.why: Yes: that is the linter's job.

choices.text: Questions about what the change does
choices.why: Those are a large part of what it is for.

choices.text: Proving the reviewer is more senior
choices.why: Yes: gatekeeping.

choices.text: Being the only defence against bugs
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Match each Conventional Comments label to what it means.

pairs.right: the reviewer is asking, not hinting
a better way the author may decline
trivial; take it or leave it

prompt: Called at 21:10, how many of the three windows Rafael's function returned were after the depot's 22:00 closing?
What did the labels give Rafael that five unlabelled comments would not?
hint: A new engineer reading five comments.

choices.text: Proof that Diego had read the whole change carefully
choices.why: Not what labels are for.

choices.text: A way to skip the comments marked nitpick without reading them at all
choices.why: They are still read; they are just optional.

choices.text: Which one blocked the merge
choices.why: Right: without labels, five comments read as five demands.

choices.text: A shorter review, since labels replace explanations
choices.why: Labels add a word; the explanation stays.

prompt: A reviewer writes "Did you consider using a dict here?" meaning "use a dict". What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Write it as a suggestion, and ask only when you don't know
choices.why: Right: Diego's Saturday question was real, and its answer found a second issue.

choices.text: Mark it as an issue so the author has to change it
choices.why: Only if it must be fixed before merging.

choices.text: Delete it; the author should find it alone
choices.why: The reviewer noticed something worth saying.

choices.text: Keep it as a question, since questions are gentler
choices.why: A command in disguise confuses more than it softens.

prompt: Why does the lesson say "LGTM" teaches nothing?

choices.text: Approvals should always come with at least one issue
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: It is impolite to the author
choices.why: Tone is not the issue.

choices.text: It is an acronym, so the author may not know what it means
choices.why: Everybody knows it; it says nothing specific.

choices.text: It does not say which choices to keep making
choices.why: Right: specific praise is calibration.

prompt: What did the SmartBear study at Cisco find about large reviews?

choices.text: Defect-finding fell sharply past about 400 lines
choices.why: Right: past a size, reviewers scroll instead of reading.

choices.text: Large reviews found more defects per line
choices.why: The opposite.

choices.text: Size made no difference if the reviewer was senior
choices.why: Not a finding the lesson reports.

choices.text: Reviews over 400 lines should be rejected automatically by the tooling
choices.why: The study measured; it did not set rules.

prompt: Put the blocks of Rafael's pull request description in order.
items: What is not in this PR

prompt: What does the "Not in this PR" block prevent?

choices.text: The obvious question, answered in advance
choices.why: Right: "what about holidays?" never needs to be asked.

choices.text: A second review later
choices.why: The holiday change will be reviewed on its own.

choices.text: Scope creep, by forbidding new requests
choices.why: It names what was left out; it forbids nothing.

choices.text: Anybody merging the PR before the holidays are added
choices.why: It does not block the merge.

prompt: Rafael disagrees with one of Diego's suggestions. By the lesson, what should he do?

choices.text: Accept it, since the reviewer has the final word
choices.why: A suggestion may be declined.

choices.text: Ignore it and merge once approved
choices.why: Every comment gets an answer.

choices.text: Decline it, with a reason about the code
choices.why: Right: disagreeing with a reviewer is part of the job.

choices.text: Escalate to Henrique before replying
choices.why: A suggestion is not a conflict needing a lead.

prompt: What is Lívia's rule of thumb for learning comments when reviewing a junior?

choices.text: At most one per review
choices.why: Right: correctness issues always get a comment; learning ones are rationed so each is heard.

choices.text: None until the junior has been on the team for six months
choices.why: No waiting period in the lesson.

choices.text: Only praise, to protect confidence
choices.why: Praise matters and is not the whole review.

choices.text: Comment on every issue found, so nothing is missed
choices.why: Twenty comments bury the two that matter.

prompt: Which comment points rather than solves?

choices.text: "Change line 12 to a comprehension."
choices.why: A solution handed over.

choices.text: "There's a table of opening hours. Can you find it?"
choices.why: Right: it names what exists and leaves the finding to the author.

choices.text: "Why did you do it like this, instead of the way we usually do?"
choices.why: Reads as "this is wrong", with nothing to go on.

choices.text: "This is wrong. Use the opening-hours table instead of the constant."
choices.why: Solves, and sounds harsh.

prompt: Why does the lesson suggest "we" for the codebase in written comments to a junior?
hint: A comment is read louder than written.

choices.text: It shares the blame for the mistake
choices.why: There is no blame to share in a review.

choices.text: It talks about the code, not the person
choices.why: Right: a short comment from a senior person is read as harsher than intended.

choices.text: It is the company's style guide
choices.why: Not a rule; a habit for tone.

choices.text: It is shorter than naming the author
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

prompt: A new engineer's first pull request has twelve small problems and one that would corrupt orders. What does this lesson suggest?
hint: Correctness always; learning rationed; sometimes together.

choices.text: Thirteen comments, so that she sees every problem at once and learns
choices.why: The one that matters gets buried.

choices.text: Fix all thirteen yourself and approve
choices.why: The change gets fixed and the author learns nothing.

choices.text: Approve with "LGTM" to encourage her on her very first pull request
choices.why: It ships the bug that corrupts orders.

choices.text: Block on the order bug, add one learning note, and offer a call
choices.why: Right: correctness gets its comment, the rest is chosen, and a first PR is worth reading together.
